text:
anya: heads-up — during a small net ops window in eu we saw a weird class of streaming sessions (SSE and WS) that remain TCP-up but stop receiving frames for 20-90s, then resume. console didn’t show socket closed.

sam: do we have a sample trace or tenant list?

anya: trace id b4d7c2 -> https://console/redwood/trace/b4d7c2. dev-bot fired an alert `streaming.silent-output` at 2026-03-12T09:12Z. affected tenants: corp-99, small-333.

ryan: initial thought: our proxy introduced a transient "quiesce" mode during the TLS rekey to avoid spamming pings to backends. the proxy sets `x-proxy-quiesce: 1` and suppresses ping frames. clients rely on application-level heartbeats so they stayed connected.

tina: product note: interactive chat apps are unhappy — spinner persists and resumed tokens are not always surfaced by the frontend. they want a deterministic UX.

sam: can we see raw socket timeline? tcpdump show no FIN/RST, but app-level frames absent. proxy logs show `quiesce_enter` / `quiesce_exit` events around the same time as `tls_rekey`.

anya: repro curl we used (SSE):

```curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://eu-api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=chat-lite"```

When quiesce starts, server-side event queue continues to advance (last-event-id increments in logs) but nothing is flushed to socket until quiesce_exit. clients see an unexplained gap.

dev-bot: ALERT streaming.silent-output spike -> 63 events in 15m (eu). top routes: /v1/streams, /v1/chat/stream.

ryan: tradeoff background: quiesce avoids thundering reconnects during rekeys and reduces backend churn/cost. downside: silent stalls break UIs.

tina: product asks if we can make resumed frames include a small resume marker event so clients can detect gap and update UI (e.g., send `event: resumed
data: {"gap_ms": 45000}

`).

sam: quick fixes: 1) emit `x-proxy-quiesce: 1` response header when proxy enters quiesce; 2) runtime to emit `event: quiesce_start` / `event: quiesce_end` SSE markers around the stall; 3) console: correlate `proxy.quiesce_count` with `streaming.silent-output` and add tenant/route labels.

ryan: longer term: client heuristics vs forced reconnect. options: a) client short-circuit — if `x-proxy-quiesce` present and no frames >8s, client attempts resume; b) server-forced-resume — on quiesce_end, server sends an explicit resume marker and maybe a small prefix replay; c) keep as-is.

tina: product prefers (b) + (a) fallback. they don’t want forced reconnects that double-invoice tokens but do want the UI to clearly reflect a gap and then continue.

anya: metrics request: add `proxy.quiesce_duration_seconds` histogram, `streaming.silent_output_duration` gauge, and label both with `route`, `tenant_id`, `model_family`. ops needs that to pinpoint customers.

sam: ops mitigation: temporarily reduce quiesce aggressiveness for eu region (quiesce_threshold -> 0.3) while we iterate. I'll open a canary flag. also increasing trace sampling to 12% for 2h.

ryan: engineering worklist:
- runtime: emit `x-proxy-quiesce` header and SSE markers (quiesce_start/end)
- client SDK: treat `quiesce_start` marker as special and surface a non-blocking spinner; if no marker available, fallback to stall->resume heuristic (8s default)
- telemetry: add labeled metrics and dashboard tile linking quiesce vs silent-output alerts
- ops: canary threshold rollback + ramped tracing

anya: created runbook RB-3301, owners: anya(investigate), sam(telemetry/flags), ryan(runtime), tina(product/comm). target hotfix today, full change in next minor.

dev-bot: Runbook RB-3301 created and assigned.

sam: I'll post slices and add a console banner for tenants impacted. ops will watch error budget and billing anomalies.

ryan: note for engineers — be careful with replay semantics. if we try to replay missed tokens at resume time we risk duplicate outputs for some customers (stateless vs stateful prompts). prefer explicit resume marker + idempotent hint over blind replay.

tina: customer comms: we'll offer brief explanation + mitigation steps and monitor.

anya: thanks all. starting on traces and a small runtime patch to emit headers/markers. will update RB-3301 with results. :thumbsup:
